claim: The European Commission fined Apple €500 million on 23 April 2025 for breaching DMA Article 5(4) anti-steering obligations (Case DMA.100109).
scope_conditions: EU App Store, DMA enforcement, decision date 23 Apr 2025
quoted_support: On April 23, 2025, Apple and Meta were both found to be non-compliant with the law and fined €500 million and €200 million, respectively.

claim: Apple's post-decision compliance workaround replaced up-to-17% linkout fees with a 5% initial acquisition fee plus 10% ongoing store services fee on off-App-Store purchases within 12 months of install.
stance_target: App Store economics measured effect in EU
quoted_support: Apple made an update allowing app developers more freedom to promote offers within the app, but imposed a 5% "initial acquisition fee" and an ongoing 10% "store services fee" on purchases made via link-outs.

claim: The Commission found Apple's steering compliance measures were not objectively necessary or proportionate and ordered removal of technical and commercial restrictions on steering without fees.
stance_target: lock-in as durable/structural moat justifying premium multiple
quoted_support: the Commission has ordered Apple to remove the technical and commercial restrictions on steering and to refrain from perpetuating the non-compliant conduct in the future, which includes adopting conduct with an equivalent object or effect.

claim: The EC closed its investigation into Apple's browser-choice-screen and default-settings obligations after Apple's iOS 17.4/August 2024 changes, including making Safari uninstallable.
stance_target: regulation can materially change platform defaults (partial support for inertia-not-preference view)
quoted_support: users can now uninstall several Apple pre-installed apps, such as Safari — a functionality previously unavailable.

claim: Epic Games documented that more than 50% of attempts to install the Epic Games Store on Android or iOS failed due to Apple/Google 'scare screens,' with an additional 5 million EU install attempts blocked by Apple's eligibility requirements.
stance_target: alternative app store adoption in the EU is meaningful
scope_conditions: EU iOS/Android alternative app store installs
quoted_support: more than 50% of the time a player tries to install the Epic Games Store on Android or iOS, they are unsuccessful due to onerous scare screens. In the European Union, an additional 5 million attempts to install the Epic Games Store were blocked by Apple's browser and operating system 'Eligibility Requirements.'

claim: Apple's Core Technology Fee (€0.50 per first annual install above 1 million, only for developers earning over €10M globally) is under new EC preliminary non-compliance findings as a disincentive to alternative app distribution.
stance_target: alternative app store adoption is unconstrained
scope_conditions: EU iOS alternative app store distribution
quoted_support: Developers wanting to use alternative app distribution channels on iOS are disincentivised from doing so as this requires them to opt for business terms which include a new fee (Apple's Core Technology Fee).

claim: DMA fines can reach 10% of a gatekeeper's total worldwide turnover, with periodic penalties up to 5% of average daily worldwide turnover; the €500M Apple fine is well below this ceiling.
quoted_support: The fines issued are well below the thresholds the DMA stipulates, which can reach 10% of a gatekeeper's total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year.
numbers: 5% of average daily worldwide turnover for periodic penalties
